rationale:
The `{cite}` of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` on `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]` is appropriate.

- **Not a test.** `UsageLog` is a plain struct, so `{test}` does not apply.
- **Not an `{impl}` root.** The struct holds the `UsageRecord` and the `path` it is saved to. The record's fields, such as `run_id`, `subject_kind`, `evidence_output`, `evidence_written`, `outcome` and `determination`, are defined in `struct[UsageRecord]`, not in this struct. The requirement is already implemented by marked items in `src/authoring/mod.rs`: `fn[author_evidence_with_output]`, `fn[prepare_assessment]`, and `impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]` and `fn[failed]`. I did not read these items, so I did not confirm that they use `UsageLog`. I inferred that from `UsageLog` being the type that holds the record and its save path. Code reached through marked items needs no `{impl}` of its own.
- **Not redundant.** `UsageLog` carries no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to this requirement. The `{test}` references in this file sit on test functions in `mod[tests]`, not on the struct.
- **The cite is right.** The struct holds the per-run record and its storage `path`. It also carries state that feeds the requirement's lifecycle fields, namely start and end timing, an active request and the first-request callback. A change to the requirement's storage location, record contents or lifecycle could require changing this struct, so it relies on the requirement.

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
